issues.description: The UML in the problem statement marks the Animal constructor as private (shown with '-' visibility), which would prevent subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat) from calling super(name). The solution and the intended design require the Animal constructor to be accessible to subclasses (solution uses a public constructor). This inconsistency could confuse students about the correct visibility and, if followed literally, would make implementing the subclass constructors impossible.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML and any problem text to show the Animal constructor with non-private visibility (protected or public), e.g., 'protected Animal(String)' or 'public Animal(String)', and mention that subclasses must be able to call super(name). This aligns the specification with the solution and prevents student confusion.
